review_notes: Shortened the first method from a full definition to its joint word-representation learning name; retained lexicon-relation regularization separately. Checked the research question and statistically significant similarity/analogy comparison. WordNet is only a background example, not explicitly identified as the used lexicon.

problem.concept: computational basis is only beginning to be probed

probabilistically inverting artificial-intelligence approaches to state estimation

contribution.concept: Bayesian theory of mind (BToM) model

task.concept: Personal involvement as a determinant of argument-based persuasion

contribution.concept: under high relevance, attitudes were influenced primarily by the quality of the arguments in the message, whereas under low relevance, attitudes were influenced primarily by the expertise of the source
This suggests that the personal relevance of an issue is one determinant of the route to persuasion that will be followed

review_notes: Restored suggests in the personal-relevance/route-to-persuasion conclusion, avoiding a strengthened assertion. Checked high-relevance argument-quality versus low-relevance expertise conditions and the three manipulated factors.

problem.concept: most of the CE toolkits are optimized for a single target language (mainly English) and, as far as we know, none of them are dedicated to this specific task and freely available

task.concept: predicting the quality of words of a SMT output

contribution.concept: statistical phrase-based translation model that uses hierarchical phrases

review_notes: Restored Hierarchical as the defining model-method qualifier from the title. Checked synchronous CFG learned without syntax and BLEU-relative 7.5-percent gain against Pharaoh, rather than an unqualified accuracy score.

task.concept: model such similarities observed in the consonant inventories

synthesis model for this network based on the general theory of preferential attachment

review_notes: Added the actually used synthesis model to method and removed systematic study from contribution because it describes the evaluation activity rather than an introduced artifact or result. Checked two-regime power law, inventory-size/preferential-attachment explanation and synthesis artifact.

problem.concept: Given metric space $M$ on $n$ points, when does a fully labelled positive-weighted tree $T$ exist on the same $n$ vertices that precisely realises $M$ using its shortest path metric

task.concept: measuring the goodness-of-fit of the minimum spanning tree to $M$

contribution.concept: if a spanning tree representation, $T$, of $M$ exists, then it is isomorphic to the unique minimum spanning tree in the weighted complete graph associated with $M$
fourth-point condition that is necessary and sufficient to ensure the existence of $T$ whenever each distance in $M$ is unique
a finite median graph, in which each geodesic distance is distinct, is simply a tree

Provided that the tie-breaking assumption holds, the fourth-point condition serves as a criterion for measuring the goodness-of-fit of the minimum spanning tree to $M$, i.e., the spanning tree-likeness of $M$
These quantities can be measured in $O(n^4)$ and $O(n^3)$ time, respectively

review_notes: Made the tree-likeness task operational by naming goodness-of-fit measurement. Checked the exact-realization question, unique-distance and tie-breaking assumptions, MST representation proof and fourth-point criterion. Verified O(n^4)/O(n^3) map respectively to tree/path quantities in adjacent source context.
